messages:
mike: Heads-up 1: saw an instance where the heatmap showed a clear tail spike for /v1/generate at 09:12, but the p95/p99 tiles on the detail panel stayed flat. Not expected.

tara: Interesting. Heatmap is sample-level while pctl tiles are from tdigest merges, right? Could be merge smoothing or an outlier trimming policy.

yusuf: Yep. We recently added an internal 'outlier_trim' step in the merge job to discard samples > 5s to avoid skew from synthetic tests. If the heatmap includes those samples but merged tdigest trims them, that would explain the mismatch.

mike: That sounds likely. The customer-runner incident at 09:11 injected a few 8-10s synthetic calls; heatmap picked them up but merge trimmed them before the p99 was computed.

claire: UX question: should heatmap and percentile tiles use the same filtering by default? Right now heatmap shows raw samples (helpful for investigation) but percentiles show "sanitized" merged values.

yusuf: Options:
- Keep current: heatmap raw, percentiles sanitized. Add provenance + "trim policy" note on the pctl tile.
- Make percentiles configurable: `metrics.trim_outliers = none|soft|hard` with default `soft` (clip >5s).
- Align both by storing a "raw_tdigest" (no trim) and a "sanitized_tdigest" and let the frontend select.

mike: I prefer explicit provenance + config. Most teams rely on p95 for SLOs, we shouldn't introduce wild variance. But we must avoid surprises where heatmap and p95 disagree.

tara: Agreed. Proposed UX: pctl badge "trim: soft (5s)" with hover: "Trim removes extreme samples (configurable per-tenant). Heatmap shows raw samples. Use 'raw' source for investigative queries." Add a small link "why are my tiles different?" to explain.

yusuf: Backend plan: expose `trim_policy` in the merged rows metadata and add a `source=raw|sanitized` query param. Add `counts_trimmed` to the metrics response so the UI can show how many samples were excluded. Minimal change: merge job already tracks trimmed_count; surface it.

claire: Tests: frontend e2e that simulates synthetic spike and asserts: heatmap shows spikes, pctl sanitized hides them, badge shows trimmed_count > 0. Also unit test verifying that `raw` vs `sanitized` source produce monotonic p50<=p95<=p99 per-source.

mike: Ops/runbook: if heatmap vs percentiles disagree, check `trim_policy` and `counts_trimmed`; if trimmed_count > 0 and traffic is legitimate, escalate to telemetry to adjust policy.

yusuf: Implementation note: trimmed samples can change SLOs if tenants expect raw percentiles. We must make tenant default `metrics.trim_policy=soft` and allow `trim_policy=none` for enterprise customers. Document in API: `/api/v1/metrics?route=...&source=sanitized|raw&trim=none|soft|hard`. Defaults remain conservative.

tara: Also add a small inline banner on SLO dashboards: "SLOs use sanitized percentiles (trim policy=soft)". That avoids accidental drift.

slo-bot: PR created: https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/10123 (expose trimmed_count, source param). Frontend PR: https://git.redwood/console/pulls/4120 (badge, tooltip, explain link).

claire: I'll own the frontend copy and e2e. mike can own runbook blurb. yusuf will land backend changes and add trimmed_count to the metrics payload.

mike: Thanks all. Let's watch for confusion tickets after deploy; hopeful this will make the behavior explicit and avoid the "why is heatmap screaming but p95 silent" questions. :coffee:
